summary: Careful, preregistered paired study with strong artifact grounding and appropriate preregistration fidelity. Execution and analysis appear consistent with the frozen plan; the primary inferential null result (exact two‑sided McNemar p=0.0625) is reported appropriately and exploratory one‑sided analyses are explicitly labeled. Key reproducibility artifacts (preregistration, master prompt reference, raw outputs, validator traces, analysis artifacts and hashes) are present. Primary concerns are manuscript presentation items (Disclosure Statement verbosity and References format) and a small potential for reader confusion from presenting a preregistered bootstrap CI that excludes zero alongside a non‑significant primary test; the authors already note this but should tighten wording to avoid misinterpretation.
critical_issues: Disclosure Statement duplicates execution/accounting detail and reads like an execution log rather than a concise required disclosure; it must be condensed while preserving the mandatory master_prompt locator and its SHA‑256 and the preregistration identifier and affirmation of no post‑lock manual editing.

References section includes identifier‑style entries (arXiv/SSRN/OpenAlex/DOI strings) rather than a conventional IEEE‑style bibliography with full bibliographic metadata for each cited record; the manuscript must present a standard numbered IEEE reference list where each entry supplies author(s), title, venue, year, and DOI/URL when available.

Presenting a preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI that excludes zero alongside a preregistered two‑sided McNemar test that is not significant can be misleading to readers. Although the manuscript already flags the bootstrap as descriptive and the one‑sided test as exploratory, the text should be tightened to make the inferential hierarchy and practical interpretation unambiguous.
required_revisions: Condense the Disclosure Statement to a concise paragraph that preserves (a) declared model(s) and provider(s), (b) orchestration/validator names, (c) immutable initial master prompt locator and exact SHA‑256 (provenance/master_prompt.txt), (d) preregistration identifier (cand-003-stud-001) and statement that it was frozen prior to model calls, and (e) the statement that no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. Remove or relocate execution/accounting numbers, per‑episode logs, stage counts, and artifact paths (these may remain in the archived evidence bundle and need not appear in the disclosure).

Replace the current References list with a conventional IEEE‑style numbered bibliography. For each cited work include full bibliographic metadata (authors, paper title, venue or repository, year, and DOI/URL where available). Do not leave bare DOI/arXiv/OpenAlex identifier entries; use the archived terminal_bibliographic_records to produce full entries.

Revise the Results/Discussion wording to further emphasize the inferential primacy of the preregistered two‑sided McNemar test and to avoid any insinuation that the bootstrap CI or post‑hoc one‑sided test overturns the preregistered null. A single concise explanatory paragraph (resolvable from archived artifacts) should state why the bootstrap CI can exclude zero under extremely sparse discordant counts, and reiterate that the confirmatory inference follows the preregistered exact McNemar outcome.
optional_revisions: Consider adding a short highlighted table or appendix paragraph (one paragraph only) summarizing the five discordant pairs (pair IDs and brief failure reason codes) to illustrate repair modes; this can be populated directly from terminal_factual_accounting and archived artifacts.

Briefly expand the Threats to Validity subsection to note more explicitly whether the high baseline validity likely reflects model capability, corpus characteristics, or validator permissiveness and which archived artifacts could be inspected to adjudicate among those possibilities.
